course_name_original: C.I. SCIENZA E TECNOLOGIA DEI BIOMATERIALI (TO0042)
course_name_en: Integrated Course: Biomaterials Science and Technology
prerequisites: Knowledge of basic subjects: physics, chemistry, anatomy and histology

learning_outcomes.text: Provide the student with basic knowledge of dental materials in chemical, physical and biological terms and above all in clinical application.

Present the fundamental knowledge of the manufacturing procedures, the indications for use, the components constituting the individual dental materials, their use in dentistry, in order to guide the student in the choice of materials in relation to optimal clinical use.

Acquisition of guiding concepts useful for quickly orienting oneself in the choice of materials and biomaterials among the numerous products and technologies available in the dental field in order to choose the most performing materials for clinical use.
Provide the foundations for each student to develop their research skills on the main electronic databases in the dental materials sector.

Encourage cooperation in groups and active interaction with the teacher through participation in open lectures, seminars, the discussion of scientific articles, and the critical evaluation of specific scientific literature.

syllabus_topics: New Technologies And Eco-Sustainable Materials In Dentistry

Evaluation of the properties and clinical application of dental materials for dental use. Specifically: impression materials, plasters, waxes, adhesive systems, whitening systems, composites, CAD-CAM materials, ceramics, implantology materials, biomaterials.
Guide to the study of scientific literature.
Dental ceramics: introduction, historical background, definition, and classifications. Chemical-physical structure of glass ceramics, reinforced glass ceramics, and crystalline ceramics.
Production methods of glass ceramics, reinforced glass ceramics, and crystalline ceramics, and their clinical indications.

Chemical-physical properties of dental ceramics (chemical, thermal, electrical, optical properties, hardness, mechanical strength, modulus of rupture, fracture toughness) and their behavior (fatigue, wear, scratching, chipping).
Insights from the scientific literature on chemical-physical properties.

Surface determinants (surface energy, wettability, roughness), biological properties (biocompatibility, immunogenicity, interactions with epithelial, connective, periodontal, and peri-implant tissues and with oral microorganisms) and biological behavior (epithelial adhesion, fibroblast response and adhesion, microbial adhesion and biofilm formation) of dental ceramics.
Insights from the scientific literature on biological properties and behavior.
teaching_methods: Practical exercises involving viewing and handling certain dental materials
Simulation of clinical applications of the main materials used in dentistry
Critical evaluation of specific scientific literature
assessment_rules: Learning outcomes will be assessed through a mid-term examination and a final written examination. The final grade will be awarded on a scale of thirty points (out of 30), in accordance with the assessment criteria established by the integrated course. The overall exam type for the C.I. is Written and Oral Combined.
